name: Gödel’s incompleteness results
description: Gödel showed limits to formal derivability and internal consistency proofs in specified mathematical systems powerful enough to express arithmetic.

impact.note: Known to logicians and mathematicians, it showed formal systems have provable limits, and computability and proof theory grew from it.

date.label: 26 August 1930
date.basis: Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy historical account dates Gödel’s private disclosure to Carnap.

events.statement: Gödel disclosed his incompleteness results to Rudolf Carnap.
events.scope: A private disclosure; the precise content conveyed is not established here.
events.caveats: The first theorem was publicly announced in September 1930 and the 1931 paper included a statement of the second theorem.

evidence.supports: Reports Gödel disclosed his results to Carnap on 26 August 1930 and announced the first theorem publicly on 7 September.

date.label: 7 September 1930
date.basis: Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy dates the public conference announcement.

events.statement: Gödel announced the first incompleteness result during discussion at the Königsberg conference.
events.scope: Announcement of the first theorem, not a public announcement of both theorems.

evidence.supports: Reports Gödel disclosed his results to Carnap on 26 August 1930 and announced the first theorem publicly on 7 September.

contributions.resource: Proved and published formal incompleteness results.

earliest_record.rationale: The historically reported private disclosure precedes both the public first-theorem announcement and the 1931 paper; its precise contents are unresolved.

caveats: The original proof concerns a particular formal system and specified extensions; the modern broad theorem relies on later work and appropriate assumptions. The precise content of the August 1930 private disclosure is not established here; the first theorem was publicly announced in September, and the 1931 article contained a statement of the second.
